title: Fix Pinata directory upload multipart payload and preserve correct metadata image URIs

requirements.summary: Adjust Pinata directory upload multipart/form-data payload so multi-file directory pin succeeds with JWT Bearer auth and preserves detailed HTTP error diagnostics.
acceptanceCriteria: From the Vault publishing flow, uploading a typical full generated collection (images + metadata) completes successfully and returns a directory CID for images and a CID for the metadata JSON.
The request remains a POST to https://api.pinata.cloud/pinning/pinFileToIPFS with Authorization: Bearer <JWT> (no endpoint or auth mechanism changes).
If the directory upload still fails for any reason, the UI error message includes both the HTTP status code and the response body text (when available), preserving the existing diagnostics behavior.

file_operations.description: Fix uploadDirectoryToPinata to match Pinata directory-upload expectations by ensuring all uploaded parts represent a single directory (e.g., applying a consistent directory prefix in each file’s multipart filename / filepath semantics) rather than multiple top-level files that trigger the 400 "More than one file and/or directory was provided for pinning." error. Keep the request as POST to https://api.pinata.cloud/pinning/pinFileToIPFS with Authorization: Bearer <JWT>. Also improve error extraction to include HTTP status code and response body text (when available) without losing existing diagnostic detail.

Update uploadCollectionToIPFS to use the revised uploadDirectoryToPinata contract (including any returned directory path prefix information, if introduced) while keeping progress reporting and overall publishing flow intact. Ensure failures still surface the underlying status code + response body text coming from the Pinata utility so the UI diagnostics remain informative.

requirements.summary: Ensure generated metadata image URIs correctly reference the uploaded image directory CID and any directory prefix introduced by the directory-upload payload change, without changing token numbering behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: After a successful upload, at least one sampled token’s metadata image field resolves to an existing file under the returned images directory CID using the expected token filename convention (e.g., 0.png / 1.png depending on settings).
No regressions to existing token numbering behavior (startTokenNumberAtZero continues to affect filenames/URIs consistently).

file_operations.description: Update buildMetadataForNFT (and any related helpers) to support composing image URIs that include the returned image directory CID plus the correct relative path when a directory prefix is used (e.g., ipfs://<imageDirCID>/<prefix>/<tokenId>.png). Preserve existing startTokenNumberAtZero behavior for filename/URI token numbering.

Wire any new directory prefix/path information from the image directory upload step into metadata generation so metadata always points to the correct ipfs://<imageDirCID>/<relative path>. Keep existing tokenId filename convention logic consistent with startTokenNumberAtZero.
